# 5.3 · Decoding Knobs

`Level 5: Attention Is Weighted Averages` · `+25 XP` · `drill 3 of 3`

## The job
Write the controls that turn next-token probabilities into an actual choice. `greedy`
picks the most likely index (ties go to the lowest index). `top_k_filter` keeps the k most
likely tokens and renormalises. `top_p_filter` keeps the smallest set of most-likely tokens
whose probabilities add up to at least p. `sample` draws an index with a seeded RNG.
`decode_step` chains them: softmax with temperature, optional top-k, optional top-p, sample.

## Why it matters
The same model can sound robotic, creative or unhinged depending only on these knobs. When
someone says "set temperature to 0 for evals" or "top-p 0.9 for chat", this is the code they
mean. Seeded sampling is also how you make a stochastic system reproducible enough to test.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 5.3     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 5.3      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. Rank tokens with `sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (-probs[i], i))` so ties are broken by index.
2. Filters return a new list of the same length with zeros for dropped tokens, renormalised to sum to 1.
3. For top-p, walk the ranked tokens adding probabilities and stop right after the running total reaches p.
4. `sample`: draw r = rng.random(), then return the first index where the running total exceeds r. Skip zero-probability tokens so they can never be chosen.
5. `kit.mathx.softmax` handles temperature for you in `decode_step`.

</details>
